part.text:
All 15 test cases pass and `go vet` is clean. `markdown_test.go` was not touched and no new files were created. ## What I did The spec (`.docs/instructions.md`) is a refactoring exercise: the original `markdown.go` walked the input byte-by-byte while juggling five intertwined flags (`header`, `pos`, `list`, `listOpened`, `he`) plus fragile index comparisons like `strings.LastIndex(markdown, "\n") > strings.LastIndex(markdown, "*")`. I traced its exact behavior against every test case and rewrote it around the three ideas the parser actually uses: 1. **`expandEmphasis`** — the first `__` pair becomes `` and the first `_` pair becomes `` (strong first, so bold markers aren't eaten by the italic pass), done once up front on the whole input. 2. **Line-oriented processing** — the input is split into lines, and each line is exactly one of: a list item, a header, or a paragraph. 3. **One list state variable** — `inList` opens `
    ` on the first `* ` line, stays open across consecutive items, and closes when a non-list line or end-of-input is reached. This cleanly replaces the old `list` counter + `listOpened` flag + `LastIndex` hacks (e.g. the "End a list" case). Supporting helpers: `listItemText` (detects `* ` items), `renderBlock` (1–6 leading `#` → `…`, more than 6 → literal paragraph text, else `

    …

    `), and `leadingHashes`. The refactoring notes explaining all of this are in comments in `markdown.go`, as the spec suggested.
